description.purpose: A session as a channel GENERATION, modelled on a phone call: it begins with a turn, it ends deterministically, and the fluid transition in between belongs to it. The keeper mints the id at the surface and stamps every inbound turn with it, keeps one idle clock per channel, and ends a generation at night by arithmetic -- a timer plus an idle threshold, never a model judgement. Reopening is lazy: nothing pre-creates a session, the next turn opens the next generation by itself. Since 2.2.0 the ledger writes itself out ([#555](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/555)): `./sessions` writes its own `seed/sessions.jsonl` through the substrate's `transfer` slot, inside the fence it declares in `params.transfer.base_path`, and `./porter` says `export_done` off the slot's own receipt -- four levels up nothing files anything any more. Since 2.2.0 its three behaviour knobs are params too ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138)): the idle window and the seal guard of `./close`, and the nightly cron inside `./night`'s own schedule -- so two keepers in one colony end their sessions on different rules, which a colony-wide environment could not say.
description.use_when: In front of an agent's context assembly, wherever a conversation needs a beginning and an end instead of one endless thread -- a day boundary for the window, a scope for the episode a memory hive is handed, an anchor for 'this call' versus 'yesterday'. Wire the ingress lane, the stamped-turn exit and the close port in the SAME mutation that instantiates it; an island without a crossing edge stays inactive. Since 2.1.0 the hive also carries a TRANSFER lane: `in_export` hands the session ledger out as a versioned document and `in_import` takes one back into a running keeper. Wire both drains (`dump` and `reject`) in the same mutation as the ingress -- `params.required_drains` refuses it otherwise (GH #471).
description.not_in_scope: No context assembly and no conversation content: the turns live in the collector's window, and the keeper never reads them. No summary and no memory write -- the close request says WHICH generation ended, never what it was worth; who reads the day out of which store is the consumer's business. No model anywhere: whether a conversation is over is decided by silence and a clock, and the LLM variant of that question is a later experiment. Nothing is deleted; a sealed generation keeps its row.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./stamp, ./close, ./sessions or ./night is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route. Entry (the parent edge names the lane with set_hop route and promotes the channel identity to context.channel AND the round to context.audience_set): in_turn (an inbound turn from the surface). Optional second entry, same address: in_sweep, an operator-forced sweep outside the night. Exit (from the hive path, on hop.route): 'turn' -> the context assembly (promote hop.session_id to context on that edge; that IS the stamp), 'close' -> the consumer of a finished session (the collector's in_close lane; promote hop.session_id, hop.channel AND hop.audience_set - three keys, always present and empty when unknown, because a failed CEL modifier skips the edge and a close that could not name its round would vanish instead of being refused; a batch that arrives without the round is refused downstream with missing_audience, GH #273).
three turns on tg:42 within the hour: one session id on all three, and the third turn's idle clock is the one the night reads
22:00 UTC (00:00 CEST) and tg:42 last spoke at 20:10: the generation is sealed and ONE close request leaves; the eleven further firings of that night find nothing
next morning, tg:42 says something: no session is open, so this turn mints tg:42-<its own timestamp> and the new generation runs

moving a keeper to a second colony: `in_export` produces ONE part, `sessions.jsonl`, and a keeper born from it knows which generation each channel was in. The channels themselves belong to the member rather than to this hive, so a transfer into a colony whose channel names differ carries history whose referent is gone -- see the README, 'Known limits'
